response.sql: SELECT AVG(TG) AS avg_tg, AVG(WBC) AS avg_wbc FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5;

assumptions.assumption: "Ignore missing values" means each average skips NULLs in its own column (SQL AVG default), so a row with WBC > 6.5 but a NULL TG still counts toward the average WBC and is excluded only from the average TG. The average is returned unrounded as a single row.

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignore missing values" means dropping any row where TG is missing, so both averages use the same set of rows (WBC > 6.5 and TG not null).
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(TG) AS avg_tg, AVG(WBC) AS avg_wbc FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 AND TG IS NOT NULL;

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignore missing values" means dropping any row where TG is missing, so both averages use the same set of rows (WBC > 6.5 and TG not null).
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(TG) AS avg_tg, AVG(WBC) AS avg_wbc FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 AND TG IS NOT NULL;
